items.stem: Why must electricity supply and demand be balanced continuously on the grid?

options.text: The grid stores almost no energy, so imbalance shows up instantly as a frequency deviation
options.rationale: Without large inherent storage, any mismatch changes system frequency immediately.

options.text: Because wires hold a day's worth of electricity as a buffer
Because consumers are billed only once per year
options.rationale: Billing frequency is unrelated to real-time balancing.

options.text: Because voltage is irrelevant to stability
options.rationale: Voltage and frequency are both central to stability.

items.explanation: Without large inherent storage, any mismatch changes system frequency immediately.

items.stem: Which TWO are examples of grid flexibility or ancillary services? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Demand response that shifts EV charging away from the peak
options.rationale: Demand response is a recognised flexibility service.
Batteries providing frequency response is an ancillary service.
Cosmetic changes provide no grid service.

items.explanation: Demand response is a recognised flexibility service.

items.stem: A feeder with many rooftop solar homes shows voltage rising above limits at midday. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Reverse power flow from local solar export pushing voltage up
options.rationale: Exported solar can raise local voltage beyond limits at times of low demand.

options.text: Everyone switching on electric heaters at midday
options.rationale: Heating load would lower, not raise, voltage and is unlikely at midday.
That would cause an outage, not a voltage rise.
Meters measure, they do not generate power.

items.explanation: Exported solar can raise local voltage beyond limits at times of low demand.
